{{short description|Dutch mathematician}}[[File:Frederik Schuh.jpg|thumb|Frederik Schuh]]
'''Frederik Schuh''' (7 February 1875, [[Amsterdam]] – 6 January 1966, [[The Hague]]) was a Dutch mathematician.

==Career==

He completed his PhD in algebraic geometry from Amsterdam University in 1905, where his advisor was [[Diederik Johannes Korteweg]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=74731}}</ref> He taught at the Technische Hoogeschool at Delft (1907–1909 and 1916–1945) and at Groningen (1909–1916).<ref>[[The Universal Book of Mathematics]]</ref>

==Works==

He was the inventor of the [[Chomp]] game and wrote ''The Master Book of Mathematical Recreations'' (1943).
